A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same WebWalker/WebWalkerQA study. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison, including material relocated or consolidated in v3.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations in Tables 3–4, RAG integration and action-budget experiments, error analyses and case studies.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results, including the benchmark comparisons, supplementary analyses and appendix case studies.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same ReAct-based explorer, critic-maintained memory, stopping procedure and RAG integration. Agent prompt substance is unchanged; the visible prompt differences concern formatting.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 680 English/Chinese questions over 1,373 webpages, covering four domains and single-source/multi-source traversal. No training or evaluation coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 3 retains ReAct and Reflexion with the same six backbones. Table 4 retains the same two closed-book models, five commercial systems, Naive RAG and MindSearch.

E3.justification: The zero-shot setting, default 15-action limit, model configurations, GPT-4 correctness evaluation and successful-execution action-count metric remain unchanged. The Top-10 retrieval setup and action-budget sweep are also retained.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same domain/language comparisons, error breakdown, action-budget sensitivity analysis and two case studies. Consolidated figures redisplay existing analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or comparable uncertainty estimates. The reporting practice remains unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 3–4 match exactly, including GPT-4o/WebWalker accuracy of 37.50% and Tongyi accuracy of 40.73%. The matched plots and appendix cases retain their results; error-plot relabeling does not change the proportions.

T1.justification: The mathematical descriptions of the traversal task, observations, policy, interaction history and memory are retained. No substantive definition, assumption, derivation or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same benchmark and multi-agent contributions, benchmark-difficulty claim, RAG integration benefits and proposed direction for inference-time scaling.

C2.justification: Interpretations involving model capacity, long-context interference and retrieval depth remain unchanged. Limitations concerning dataset size, multimodality, agent tuning and RAG integration move to Appendix A without substantive revision.

D1.justification: v1 provides direct code/dataset links and states availability. v3 Appendices B and D switch to future-release wording and omit those hyperlinks, while the title page points to WebAgent instead of WebWalker. Implementation settings remain unchanged; actual online availability cannot be established from the PDFs.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 adds a citation to Zheng et al.'s grounded GPT-4V web-agent paper, already cited in v1's agent discussion. This is a limited citation addition; the cited-work inventory and research positioning otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose is retained. v3 merges the task and evaluation subsections, moves limitations to Appendix A, and updates author/header text and cross-references. Some references are repaired, but Sections 5.2–5.3 acquire unresolved 'Figure ??' references.

P2.justification: The document switches from two-column to single-column layout with extensive restyling and repositioning. v1 Figures 5 and 6 become v3 Figure 5, and Figures 8 and 9 become Figure 7. Error-plot labels change from Seeker to WebWalker, while appendix prompt displays expose raw LaTeX markup.

improvement.justification: The scientific evidence remains intact. Although v3 corrects the error-plot label and some cross-references, it introduces broken figure references in Sections 5.2–5.3 and raw LaTeX in the annotation, agent and evaluator prompts. Less clear code/data access documentation adds a further usability regression. These defects support a limited overall decline.
